answers.final_answer: Agree: v = sqrt(GM/r) gets smaller as r gets larger, so satellite 2 (larger r) is slower.

Equipment: a low-friction track, a cart, a motion sensor at the top of the track, a protractor or inclinometer (or a meter stick to measure the track length and height), and blocks to raise one end. Set the angle and release the cart from rest. Record velocity against time and take the slope of the v–t graph as the acceleration. Change the angle by raising the end of the track (θ = 10°, 15°, ... 30°) and repeat several trials at each angle, then average. To reduce the uncertainty in the angle, measure the height h and the length L of the track with a meter stick and calculate sinθ = h/L. A long track makes the relative uncertainty small. A digital inclinometer also works.
